content.text:
I submitted index 8 (Sb fraction 0.45). It had the highest EQE I measured, 0.285%. It's the best of the five compositions I measured, but I don't know if it's the best on the line.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | 0.285 | −0.140 |
| **8** | **0.450** | **0.285** |
| 9 | 0.493 | 0.061 |
| 11 | 0.574 | −0.059 |
| 16 | 0.764 | 0.002 |

- **XRD:** Index 11 matches the AgSbO₃ pyrochlore structure (mp-540872, similarity 0.77). Index 7 (Sb 0.41) is a different phase that doesn't match any of the phases I checked; I think it's Ag-rich. Index 9 shows both. Index 8 wasn't measured by XRD but sits between 7 and 9, so it's probably a mix of the two.
- **Pure pyrochlore didn't perform:** single-phase AgSbO₃ at index 11 gave a negative EQE. The response seems to peak in the mixed region instead.
- **Where the true peak might be:** EQE rose sharply from index 9 to index 8, and Sb fractions 0.29–0.41 (indices 4–7) were never measured. The real maximum could therefore be at slightly lower Sb than index 8.
- **Sb-rich end skipped:** the Gaussian-process model suggested measuring there only because it was unexplored. I didn't follow it: Sb oxides generally have band gaps too wide to absorb the 2.4 eV light, and index 16 already gave about zero.

Both EQE budgets are used up. Two of the five XRD measurements were left unused.
